definition.note: The shape of the homogeneous solid that maximises gravitational attraction at a boundary point: a surface of revolution with spherical equation r = a sqrt(sin(latitude)).

construction.resume: A meridian-profile surface-of-revolution row; the radial builders in math_art/curiosity_surface_generator.py (build_radial, build_fresnel) are the pattern to follow, and the parametrization is in the cited mirror chapter.

provenance.definition: Not transcribed. The record exists to state that the surface is absent and why; a fabricated equation would be worse than a null.
sources: R. Ferreol, "Solid of maximal attraction", Encyclopedie des formes mathematiques remarquables, mathcurve.com; local mirror chapter ch1205_attraction_2 (S:/data/math_art/references/websites/mathcurve/book/surfaces/ch1205_attraction_2.md).
The chapter credits the Marquis de Saint-Jacques (1750) and C. F. Gauss (1830).
